what_happened: The job asked for two things: raise the check timeout to 1800 seconds, and treat a timed-out check as an environment problem. It was rejected at the final verdict. One major finding was listed: the accepted reading does not match the request, so passing criteria do not show the request was met. No acceptance criteria are listed as unmet and no checks as failed. The stored fields don't say which part of the request the reading got wrong (the timeout value, or what "treat as an environment" should do).
cause: Nothing compares the accepted reading with the request's own words before the producer runs. A short request with a loose phrase ("treat as an environment") can be read several ways: an environment stop that holds the job, one that gets a retry, or one that just doesn't count against the job. Neither the reading step nor the critic restates the phrase in terms of existing outcomes, such as the low-disk or environment-stop handling. So the criteria are written against the reading and pass, while the request is not met. Only the verifier at the final verdict compares the reading with the request, and there rejection is the only outcome. This is an inference, since the stored fields do not show the reading.
prevention: Add a reading-vs-request check before the producer is dispatched. It would extract each distinct requirement from the request text (here: the 1800s value, and the timed-out-check-as-environment behavior). It would require every one to map to at least one acceptance criterion that names an observable outcome, such as the job's end state and its record when a check times out. Any phrase that names an outcome by a vague term must be tied to an existing end state or be flagged as a question. The check must refuse a reading that leaves a requirement unmapped.
proposed_request: Raise the check timeout to 1800 seconds. When a check times out, treat it as an environment failure, not a verdict on the work. In that case the job must not end rejected, and it must record that the check timed out and which check it was. It must follow the same path as other environment stops, such as low disk, and must not count as progress-less spend. A check that fails by returning an error must still fail the job as before. Acceptance: (1) the configured check timeout is 1800 seconds, shown by the config value and a test that reads it; (2) a test where a check exceeds the timeout shows the job does not end as a rejected verdict and records a timeout reason; (3) a test where a check fails with a non-zero exit still rejects the job; (4) existing tests pass.
